parsed.attack: The product's entire visible surface is a rising number beside your mother's name, and the author's own evidence [249] says continuity pressure is what makes people want this category switched off - 'Mum - 34 days' is continuity pressure with a counter bolted to it. The ignoring starts around the fourth weekday evening, because a Focus flip from Work to Personal is a clock edge in a costume: it fires at six, when the person is commuting, cooking or wrangling children, and a call to an ageing parent is a forty-minute emotional commitment, not a tap. After five swipes the Live Activity is lock-screen furniture and the number keeps climbing, so by week three the app is a daily notice that you are a bad son, which is the most reliably deleted object on a phone.
parsed.strongest_defence: Reset-from-actual-contact removes the loudest failure in the evidence - the prompt that fires on a day contact already happened - and three people maximum keeps the surface quiet rather than nagging; the counter can be suppressed entirely, leaving a bare call button with no number attached. The obligation is genuinely permanent, and when a parent's health declines the product's salience rises rather than decays.
parsed.verdict_reason: The idea's own cited evidence says a visible continuity counter is what makes people turn this category off, the counter is the only surface it has, and the repair - delete the number, drop the cadence - is a different product rather than a defence of this one.
